newsitem.title: UK: Britain's budget - what the Sunday papers say.
newsitem.headline: Britain's budget - what the Sunday papers say.

text.p: The run-up to budget day in Britain would not be complete without a slew of newspaper speculation about the chancellor of the exchequer's plans.

Chancellor Gordon Brown, the finance minister, has promised to tax the windfall profits of privatised utilities to fund a welfare-to-work programme and to reduce value added tax on home heating bills to five percent from eight percent.
This would be paid for by scrapping tax relief on private medical insurance for over-60s.

Apart from those measures, following is a run-down of the steps that Sunday's newspapers suspect Brown will include on his maiden budget on Wednesday. The well-off, homeowners, car drivers and smokers look set to bear the brunt.
INDEPENDENT ON SUNDAY
-- reduce sharply or even abolish mortgage interest tax relief at source (MIRAS), which lets home owners claim 15 percent tax relief on the first 30,000 stg ($49,800) of a loan.
-- raise threshold for stamp duty on house purchases to 100,000 stg from 60,000 stg and double it to two percent.
-- possible increase in ceiling on National Insurance contributions (NICs). Earnings above 24,180 stg are currently exempt.
-- two "green" taxation measures, including big rise in fuel excise duty. Company car-parking perks could also be taxed.
-- target loopholes that let firms and individuals make unlimited capital gains offshore.
SUNDAY TIMES
-- MIRAS to be phased out, not scrapped overnight.
-- a possible new tax earmarked to safeguard the National Health Service. It would probably not take effect for two years and might be set at five percent.
-- above-inflation rise in tax on cigarettes.
-- company cars to be taxed more heavily and petrol duty to rise by at least three pence per litre.

-- gradual abolition of advance corporation tax to discourage firms from paying out too much in dividends. In the same vein, more generous capital allowances for investment and research and development will be phased in over the medium term.
SUNDAY TELEGRAPH
-- raise NICs ceiling.
-- raise stamp duty on house sales and phase out MIRAS.
-- cut or abolish tax credit on dividends, now 20 percent.
OBSERVER
-- Cut in MIRAS
-- double stamp tax to two percent for more expensive homes.
-- 10 percent starting rate for tax will be left on hold.
-- scrapping of universal child benefit for those aged 16-18, to be replaced by means-tested education allowances.
-- big increases in duties on petrol, diesel and cigarettes.
-- cut in VAT on loft insulation to five from eight percent.
SUNDAY EXPRESS
-- MIRAS to be abolished.
-- possible increase in NICs.
-- possible abolition of tax credit on dividends to pay for initial move toward 10 percent starting rate of income tax.
PEOPLE
-- leaded petrol to rise two pence a litre.
-- sliding scale for annual car tax to penalise gas-guzzlers.
-- insurance tax on motor policies to rise to 17.5 percent from four percent.
-- 20 pence extra tax on a packet of cigarettes.
-- tax relief on contributions to private pensions limited to 23 percent rate.
-- beer duty may fall to compete with cheap beer from Europe, but "alcopops" (alcoholic lemonades and sodas) might be surcharged.
NEWS OF THE WORLD
-- MIRAS to be scrapped.
-- car tax disc to rise to 155 stg from 145 stg.
-- cigarettes to rise 20 pence, beer by at least five pence.
-- no action on planned 10 percent starting income tax rate.
-- relief on private pension contributions limited to 23 percent basic tax rate.
MAIL ON SUNDAY
-- abolition of tax credits on dividends.
-- possible doubling of stamp duty to two percent for more expensive homes.
-- crackdown on creative accounting and legal loopholes that let rich individuals and multi-national companies cut their tax bills.
-- 10 pence more tax on cigarettes.
-- higher excise duty on alcopops.
-- taxes on car emissions and company car parking perks.
-- lower VAT on loft insulation.
SUNDAY BUSINESS
-- a timetable will be set for 10 pence starting rate of income tax.
-- landfill tax to be increased, raising one billion stg.
-- higher petrol and diesel duties.
-- VAT to be cut on domestic insulation.
-- increased duties on cigarettes, alcohol and insurance premiums.
-- increase in stamp duty on houses to as much as seven percent.
-- Full-scale abolition of MIRAs unlikely.
-- London newsroom 44-171-542 7767 ($ = 0.601 British Pounds)
